grh_1c3a1f652c2347c2227d.title: Dr Christian For Mayor
paragraphs: John Hewitt withdraws from the Rivers End mayoral race and decides that Dr. Christian should replace him, launching a draft movement before the doctor can refuse. The town embraces the idea so enthusiastically that Christian's office becomes campaign headquarters, civic groups demand promises for playgrounds, pensions, sidewalks, fountains and lower taxes, and his medical work is increasingly disrupted. Christian wants no part of politics, but Hewitt's supporters reinterpret every refusal to campaign as proof of his devotion to duty. At the public meeting Christian finally finds a medical way to cure the town of its political fever. He describes the costly demands being made on the next mayor and then makes the voters confront the fact that electing him would also mean giving up the doctor they rely on. The crowd quickly decides it needs Dr. Christian more as a physician than as a politician. Christian gives his support to the practical and experienced Hewitt, while the town names Christian honorary mayor as an expression of affection. He accepts the honorary title happily, having preserved both his practice and his friendship with the community.

grh_1c07a3b84c6516f49ed8.title: Auto Accident
paragraphs: On a snowy New Year's Eve, newly employed Dave Fenton is struck by a hit-and-run car outside the power plant and left with a dangerous brain concussion. Wealthy Marion Brooks soon admits that her own new coupe skidded at the same curve at about the same time, damaging its rear fender, and that she drove on because she was hurrying to a party. Convinced she may have hit Dave, Marion first looks for a way her money and position can protect her, but Dr. Christian forces her to face what the Fenton family would lose. By the time she decides to confess and help them, police report that another driver, Foster, has surrendered: the parked car at the curve was hit twice, and Marion caused only the earlier collision. The narrow escape leaves her changed even though she was not the hit-and-run driver.

paragraphs: Shayne investigates a New Orleans family terrified of Anthony Carrell, a legendary voodoo figure said to have survived since the early nineteenth century and to destroy anyone who defies him.
